analysis.title: Record Tech Selling, VIX Explosion... Who Is Blowing Up
key_insights: NDX closed below its 100-day moving average and is still inside the range in place since May. It has not reached the lower end of that range. The longer-term trendline and 200-day moving average sit slightly lower. RSI is approaching extremely oversold levels.

SOX has dropped to a major support area that has held several times since May. The longer-term trendline is near these levels and the 200-day moving average sits slightly lower. SOX has not been this oversold since the Liberation Day sell-off.

Info Tech saw the biggest percentage net selling since GS records began in 2016. Tech was the most aggressively sold global sector this week, with the largest percentage cut in gross exposure in two months. Long liquidations drove most of it, with additional short sales.

Aggressive buying in VIX futures sent the VIX to its highest level since July. VVIX rose 17 points, one of its largest single-day moves in four years. Front-month VIX futures outperformed their implied sensitivity to SPX by 1.5 vol points, the biggest divergence since April per GS.

Investors had been selling volatility for income into a calm equity market because it had worked. Asset managers entered Friday's session with their largest net short position in VIX futures on record per GS, which added fuel to the vol spike.

SPX is barely off its all-time highs and has only pulled back to its 100-day moving average. The longer-term trendline, 200-day moving average and range lows sit roughly 250 points lower. The author reads the vol stress as a sign that a large participant is blowing up, and notes SPX has not tested the bottom of its range.

sector_views.rationale: Record net selling in Info Tech per GS and NDX and SOX at or near support. The author asks whether this is another positioning washout near range lows, without committing to a direction.

risk_factors: Short-volatility positioning, including a record asset manager net short in VIX futures, can unwind quickly when vol rises.
Further tech liquidation if NDX and SOX break below current support zones.
A single large participant blowing up could keep stress in vol markets elevated even though SPX is near highs.
